summary: Dedicated pool: sudden GPU starvation after autoscaler telemetry drop; noisy sidecar heartbeat implicated
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (LuminaHealth) reports a sudden drop in throughput and elevated request queueing beginning ~2026-03-11 09:30 PDT in their dedicated GPU pool (us-west). P50/P95 latency rose and many requests hit 429/503 fallback. Impact: production features serving clinical note summarization degraded across multiple endpoints.

Impact:
- Customer reports ~60% reduction in sustained throughput for pinned routes.
- P99 latency saw >5x increase for batched routes.
- Some requests failed with 503 and others were routed to lower-tier model variants.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id dcp-west-7 (reserved GPUs).
- Region: us-west-2.
- Models serving: redwood-7b-instruct (primary) with redwood-13b-quant fallback.
- Config: autoscaler with predictive window enabled, heartbeat-based slot accounting (sidecar heartbeats to scheduler).

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Customer traffic steady prior to incident; no deployment changes on customer side.
2) At 09:30 PDT, internal autoscaler logs show abrupt drop in active slot counts for dcp-west-7.
3) Scheduler began throttling allocations; new requests queued and some routed to fallback (lower capacity) models.
4) Sidecar heartbeat ingestion on scheduler metrics pipeline dropped from ~1200/s to ~20/s from nodes in pool.
5) Node-level monitoring shows CPU spikes (~85-95%) on a subset of nodes and ephemeral OOMs in sidecar process in 3/24 GPUs.

Logs / metrics (samples):
- scheduler.metrics: slot_count_active: 192 -> 48 within 90s
- autoscaler.decision: predicted_capacity_down -> action: shrink by 4 nodes at 09:32:41
- sidecar.log (node-3): "watchdog: heartbeat missed - backoff 30s" repeated
- kernel: nvlink warnings and transient PCIe latency bumps recorded in node logs around 09:33

Customer statement pasted: "We saw our latency skyrocket and about half our traffic fell back to a smaller model. No config changes from our side; this started suddenly and affected all environments in us-west."

Urgency: P0. Business-critical model endpoint impacted in production for an enterprise customer.

Requested by customer: immediate mitigation to restore throughput and follow-up on root cause and preventive action.
comments: Support (Ava): Acknowledged at 09:38 PDT. Escalating to SRE and Dedicated Ops. Notified customer of initial triage and that we are pausing non-essential maintenance windows.

SRE (Diego): Initial telemetry shows sidecar heartbeat ingestion collapse at 09:30. Hypothesis: sidecar process CPU pressure led to missed heartbeats and autoscaler inferred node emptiness, triggering shrink. Collecting /var/log/sidecar logs and kernel traces from nodes.

SRE (Priya - networking): Observed short-lived PCIe latency bumps on 3 nodes. Correlating with sidecar restarts triggered by oom-killer. Investigating background process (checkpoint writer) on those nodes.

Customer (LuminaHealth - ops): Confirmed they did not push any traffic changes. Appreciated quick update. Asked if we can fail traffic over to their reserved fallback dedicated pool in another AZ while we investigate.
Support (Ava): Provided temporary routing to reserved standby pool in us-west-2a at 10:05 PDT per customer's request; documented change and monitored for restoration of throughput.
SRE (Diego): After sidecar restarts and temporary routing, throughput returned to expected baseline by 10:42 PDT. Marking incident mitigated. Will continue root cause analysis and a patch rollout.
Customer: Requested a postmortem and confirmation of patch schedule before end of week.
investigation_notes: 09:30-09:36 PDT: sudden drop in sidecar heartbeat ingestion from ~1200/s to ~20/s limited to nodes in dcp-west-7. No upstream metric pipeline outage detected.
Collected sidecar logs show repeated 'heartbeat missed' and rapid restarts. OOM kill entries correspond to sidecar processes on 3 physical hosts.

Kernel logs include elevated PCIe error counters and nvlink speed throttles for affected hosts. Not all hosts in pool show PCIe issues. Hypothesis: background checkpoint writer process entered a pathological state causing bursty I/O, starving CPU and interfering with sidecar.

Autoscaler behavior: Given reduced heartbeat and perceived lower active slots, predictive autoscaler scheduled shrink actions. Shrink occurred faster than expected due to conservative safety thresholds when heartbeat is missing (edge-case of concurrent OOMs).

Failover and routing: fallback to 13b quant model happened per routing policy. However fallback model capacity in same pool was also constrained, causing 503s for some requests. Moving some routes to the standby pool reverted most failures.

Runbook checks performed: node health checks, container restarts, kube events, nv_peer_memory metrics, and recent infra deploys. A minor sidecar release had rolled out two hours earlier but metric suggests node-local behavior rather than a global bug.

Root cause determination: combination of (1) bursty checkpoint writer I/O causing CPU and memory pressure on a subset of hosts, (2) sidecar memory leak exacerbated by older binary on those hosts causing OOMs, (3) autoscaler shrink policy treating missed heartbeats as immediate capacity loss leading to rapid node shrink without waiting for short transient faults.
resolution_notes:
Applied immediate mitigations (2026-03-11 10:00 PDT):
- Temporarily routed high-priority customer traffic to standby dedicated pool (us-west-2a) to restore SLAs.
- Increased autoscaler heartbeat grace window from 20s -> 90s for affected pool to avoid premature shrink.
- Manually restarted sidecar processes on all affected nodes and applied temporary cgroup CPU limits to checkpoint writer to prevent IO runaways.

Short-term fix (2026-03-12):
- Rolled hotfix sidecar binary to affected hosts to resolve observed memory leak (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4571).
- Adjusted autoscaler logic to require corroborating metrics (slot usage + heartbeat) before automatic shrink when OOMs are detected.
- Added an alert to trigger automated containment of heavy local IO (block checkpoint writer) when sidecar CPU > 70% and heartbeat rate drops > 80%.

Long-term actions (post-incident):
- Formal postmortem scheduled; owner: Diego Martinez; due 2026-03-18.
- Scheduler change: implement exponential backoff to shrink decisions and require two consecutive predictive windows before node termination in dedicated pools.
- Audit of sidecar rollout pipeline to ensure canary fraction and health checks detect memory leak regressions earlier.
- Runbook update: expand dedicated-pool incident checklist with guidance to temporarily route to standby pools and manual autoscaler override steps.
- Customer follow-up: scheduled 1:1 with LuminaHealth CSM to review incident, mitigations, and timeline for permanent fixes.
Status: mitigations applied and verified; throughput restored and customer confirmed service returned to baseline. Incident marked Resolved pending postmortem.
final_resolution: Mitigated: restored customer throughput by routing to standby pool, sidecar hotfix, and autoscaler grace-window change. Permanent scheduler and sidecar rollout improvements planned; postmortem due 2026-03-18.
notes: Preserved ticket-like format for operational handoff; this record should be referenced when reviewing autoscaler shrink heuristics and sidecar canary rollouts.
